differences.what: T-2857 openings: the jambs of the four first-floor windows and the door fit the model's opening spacing camera-free (one-dimensional projective fit along the course, 10 jambs, 1.50 px rms). The openings are right relative to one another (docs/RESEARCH/glessner-prairie-front-T-2857/).

T-2857 north-end openings: HABS sheet 6 places first-floor A 0.63 ft, B 0.38 ft, the door 0.37 ft and the second-floor north group 0.30 ft further north than built, and draws the first-floor lights 4.3-4.45 ft wide against the 3.9 ft built (T-2858).

T-2857 camera: the two Prairie-corner controls are the downspouts (sheet 6 draws them 0.90 and 0.82 ft in from the corners), and through this camera every first-floor jamb lands 20.5 px left of the photograph (21.6 px rms), the stacks 15-22 px left with them. A registration error, not the building; refit on the openings with the stacks withheld (T-2858).
T-2857 roof and stacks: the three stack tops are within 2 px of the photograph (south +2, middle -1, north +1 px) and the ridge within 4-8 px; the main roof and stack heights agree.
Stone/course relief: the photograph's rock-faced courses alternate deep and shallow more strongly than the render's.
The early streetscape and neighbor geometry are separate context work; monochrome/sepia reproduction does not establish exact1904 RGB, and the courtyard is not visible.

T-2848 light: hazy, shadowless light, the Prairie front a little brighter than the 18th Street flank; the render now uses the overcast sky with its soft key from the east (camera solve.light), replacing a sun carried over with the camera and no reading behind it.
